policy_name: Guidelines for Staff on the Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence Tools

conflict_rule: Any use of AI tools must comply with applicable legal obligations, in particular the AI Act; internal tools' terms and conditions also apply.

record_provenance.notes: Text taken from the copy in asago-ai/asago-policy-mapper (policy_examples/eu-com.pdf). The copy has only 3 pages (it ends after Rule 4 on p. 3) and is partly redacted (footnotes 3, 5 and 7 and some links blacked out), so later rules, if any, are missing. Page 2 has no text layer; its text was transcribed from the page image. The document cites the AI Act as 'Regulation (EU) 2024/1624' (the AI Act is Regulation (EU) 2024/1689); recorded as EU_AI_Act_2024. Titled 'guidelines', but the content is mandatory staff rules ('Rule n°1–4', 'staff must'), so recorded as an internal policy; binding=false because it is not law. Whether a later version exists was not checked.

clauses.section: 2.1 [Rule n°1] Use Commission internal AI tools as the first choice.
clauses.original_text: For any work-related task involving generative AI, staff must use the Commission’s internal tools as the default option and follow their terms and conditions. These tools operate in controlled IT environments. External AI tools may only be considered if no suitable internal alternative is available.
clauses.object: generative AI tools for work tasks
clauses.requirement: internal tools as default; external tools only if no suitable internal alternative
clauses.condition: any work-related task involving generative AI
clauses.purpose: keep Commission information in controlled IT environments
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI tools (external third-party and Commission-internal, e.g. GPT@EC, GPT@JRC, eBriefing)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Transcribed from the page image of p. 2 (the copy has no text layer on that page); bold emphasis omitted.

clauses.section: 2.2 [Rule n°2] Do not use non-public or personal data in external AI tools and ensure proper handling of sensitive and personal data when using internal AI tools.
clauses.original_text: Never input into external AI tools any information that is not already public or any personal data (4). … However, the handling of Classified information is strictly prohibited in any generative AI tool, including Commission-internal ones.
clauses.object: non-public information or personal data (external tools); classified information (any tool)
clauses.requirement: no non-public or personal data in external tools; no classified information in any GenAI tool
clauses.exception: pre-authorised scientific projects involving evaluation, testing or benchmarking of AI (footnote 4)
clauses.purpose: prevent disclosure and reuse of internal information by service providers
clauses.affected_asset: non-public Commission information; personal data; classified information
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI tools (external third-party and Commission-internal, e.g. GPT@EC, GPT@JRC, eBriefing)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Transcribed from the page image of p. 2 (the copy has no text layer on that page); bold emphasis omitted. Footnote marker '(4)' kept.

clauses.original_text: In addition, a human review of outputs is necessary to comply with the principle of accuracy and transparency regarding the use of generative AI tools. Further, it is not permitted to subject individuals to decisions which produce legal effects based solely on automated processing.
clauses.action: review outputs; do not make solely automated decisions
clauses.object: generative AI outputs; decisions producing legal effects
clauses.requirement: human review of outputs; no solely automated decisions with legal effects
clauses.purpose: data-protection accuracy and rights of individuals
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI tools (external third-party and Commission-internal, e.g. GPT@EC, GPT@JRC, eBriefing)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Transcribed from the page image of p. 2 (the copy has no text layer on that page); bold emphasis omitted. Set in the context of personal data processing under data protection rules (Regulation 2018/1725).

clauses.section: 2.3 [Rule n°3] Always critically assess AI outputs for accuracy and bias.
clauses.original_text: Do not rely on AI tools as authoritative sources. Staff must always verify all AI-generated content, even when it appears coherent and confident, before using it further in Commission work. … Staff remain fully responsible for the final result.
clauses.object: AI-generated content incl. sources and references
clauses.requirement: verify all AI output and treat it as an initial draft; staff remain responsible
clauses.condition: before further use in Commission work
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI tools (external third-party and Commission-internal, e.g. GPT@EC, GPT@JRC, eBriefing)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Applies to internal and external tools alike.

clauses.section: 2.4 [Rule n°4] Be mindful of potential intellectual property rights violations and avoid directly replicating the output of a generative AI tool in public documents.
clauses.original_text: Always assess whether generated output might violate intellectual property rights. … Moreover, outputs from generative AI tools should not be copy-pasted in documents meant to be published. Exceptions can be considered if such output is based solely on documents owned by or duly licensed to the Commission (e.g. an official text translated via eTranslation).
clauses.action: assess IP; do not copy-paste into published documents
clauses.requirement: assess outputs for IP infringement; no direct replication in public documents
clauses.exception: output based solely on Commission-owned or duly licensed documents
clauses.applicable_systems: generative AI tools (external third-party and Commission-internal, e.g. GPT@EC, GPT@JRC, eBriefing)
clauses.interpretation_notes: Particular caution for drafting legislative texts; contact the Central IP Service when in doubt.
